newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso seen kept on tight rein by C.Bank.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso seen kept on tight rein by C.Bank.

text.p: The Philippine peso is likely to move in a narrow range on Thursday as the Central Bank keeps a tight rein on the market with its overnight borrowing rate of 24 percent, traders said.
"The market will still sell dollars," a dealer said. The Central Bank had to raise its key rate on Wednesday after the peso was hit by Thailand's de facto devaluation.
The peso, however, could be pulled down by arbitrage for swap points over a long weekend because of the holiday in New York, they said.

Traders said the Central Bank had quoted a higher bid and offer rate for the dollar to take this into account at 26.305/26.405 pesos. For deals to be settled today, the Central Bank quoted a bid and offer of 26.274/26.374.
Dealers said early deals were for settlement today, hovering around 26.369. Volume was light at $62 million.
